## Overview

```{mermaid}
%%| fig-width: 7
flowchart TB
    A[Manifesto Project corpus 2026-1<br/>full texts] --> B[Chunks of at most 20,000 tokens<br/>2,000-token overlap]
    B --> C1[claude-sonnet-4-6]
    B --> C2[gpt-4.1-mini-2025-04-14]
    B --> C3[gemini-3.5-flash]
    C1 --> D[13 scores per chunk, each with<br/>evidence status and verbatim quote]
    C2 --> D
    C3 --> D
    D --> E[Quote check: quote found verbatim<br/>in the chunk, not copied from the prompt]
    E --> F[Within model: confidence-weighted<br/>mean of the counted chunks]

    G --> H[Panel regressions, specification curve,<br/>non-standard errors]
```

## Corpus and chunks

The corpus is the Manifesto Project Dataset version 2026a with corpus release 2026-1:
**`r format(nrow(man), big.mark = ",")` manifestos** with machine-readable text from
`r length(unique(man$countryname))` countries, `r min(man$year)`–`r max(man$year)`.
A manifesto of at most 18,000 tokens is sent whole; longer ones are split into chunks of 20,000
tokens with a 2,000-token overlap. The texts are © their authors and distributed by the
[Manifesto Project (WZB)](https://manifesto-project.wzb.eu/); this site does not redistribute
them.

## Models

Every chunk is scored by three model families with the same prompt and schema at temperature 0.
The version actually served is logged for every call since October 2026; for the June 2026 calls
it was not logged. The Gemini June rows used the floating alias `gemini-flash-latest`, which an
anchor test identifies as `gemini-3.5-flash`.

```{r prov, echo=FALSE}
prov |> transmute(Model = MSHORT[model], Requested = model_requested, Endpoint = endpoint,
                  `Served version` = resolved_status, Chunks = format(chunks, big.mark = ","),
                  Share = sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * share_chunks)) |> kable(align = "lllllrr")
```

## What is scored

Per chunk, each model returns for each of thirteen dimensions a score from 0 to 10 (or none), an
evidence status (*verified*, *mixed* or *no evidence*) and a verbatim quote of 3 to 8 words with
its surrounding passage.

```{r dims, echo=FALSE}
b <- REG$blocks[[1]]
map_dfr(c(b$dims, b$derived), ~ tibble(Group = setNames(map_chr(b$groups, "label"), map_chr(b$groups, "id"))[[.x$group]],
  Dimension = .x$label, Range = sprintf("%g to %g", .x$min, .x$max), Definition = .x$description)) |> kable()
```

## From chunk scores to manifesto scores

1. **Which chunks count.** A chunk's score enters if the model rates its evidence as
   *verified* and the quote passes the quote check: it is found verbatim in the chunk and is
   not copied from the prompt. Every manifesto page shows each quote and whether it counted.
2. **Within a model:** the mean of the counted chunk scores, weighted by the model's
   confidence for that block of dimensions (populism, ideology or liberalism).
3. **Across models:** the plain mean of the available models. This is the score shown as
   *combined* and used in the paper.
4. **Ideology direction:** (right − left) / (right + left + centrist) on the combined scores,
   from −1 (left) to +1 (right).

The site recomputes these scores from the public files and checks that they equal the
replication chain's values exactly before any page is written.

## Robustness

Every defensible alternative (model subsets, within- and between-model aggregation, evidence
rules, samples, fixed effects, standard errors) is estimated; the distribution of the populism
coefficient over all specifications is the [specification curve](interactive/regression.qmd).
Results: [the Milei question](analysis/milei-question.qmd).

## Evidence on this site

Quotes are shown with their first 8 words and without the surrounding passage, to respect the
Manifesto Project's terms of use. The full model output, including longer quotes and passages, is
archived with the replication package and is not public.
